id.description: Who, precisely enough to ask them about it later: a person's email, an agent's name, the executor's identifier.
id.title: Id

ActorKind.description:
Who did this.

The distinction is load-bearing and is the reason this is an enum rather than a string. Only a
`HUMAN` may grant. An `AGENT` proposes; an `EXECUTOR` is the one code path that performs an
external action, and it acts only on a grant it has verified.
ActorKind.title: ActorKind

ApprovalEventType.description: The whole lifecycle. A proposal ends granted-then-executed, rejected, or failed.
ApprovalEventType.title: ApprovalEventType

description: One event in the log. Immutable by construction: `frozen=True`.

at.description: When, for a reader. Not the ordering (see `seq`).
at.title: At

attestation.description: HMAC over the event's canonical form. Absent only on an event that has not been signed yet; a stored event without one does not verify and is refused.
attestation.title: Attestation

content_hash.description: A hash of the proposal's payload. Carried on the proposal and on the grant, so an executor can prove the thing approved is the thing it is about to do.
content_hash.title: Content Hash

data.description: What this event is about, in the kind's own terms.
data.title: Data

id.description: The proposal this event concerns. Stable across its life.
id.title: Id

scope.description: Which log this belongs to. The Foundry Studio scopes by venture; Holy Corner scopes by the subject the approval is about.
scope.title: Scope

seq.description: Monotonic within a scope. THE ORDER OF THE LOG. Never sort these by `at`: two events a millisecond apart have an unarguable order by integer and an arguable one by clock.
seq.title: Seq

v.description: Shape version, so a reader can tell old from new.
v.title: V

title: ApprovalEvent
